subject: Order form: maintenance window & uptime credit logistics
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@pinebridge.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Pinebridge Legal <legal@pinebridge.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Order form draft - uptime targets and maintenance

Alex — thanks for the updated order form. A few items from our side that need clarity before legal signs off:

1) Maintenance windows: you currently list a weekly 02:00-04:00 UTC window. Our production traffic peaks overlap that window; can we shift to a 03:00-05:00 UTC slot or alternatively allow customer-driven scheduling for critical maintenance?

2) Uptime credits: the table references a 99.9% target with credits based on monthly availability. We need the credit calculation spelled out (per-incident cap and cumulative cap). Also propose a hard cap at 50% of monthly fees.

3) Response times: for P1 incidents we need 30-minute initial response and a clearer escalation path to engineering.

Attaching our annotated copy (highlights are legal redlines). Happy to hop on a call later this week.

Best,
Elena Torres
Director of Platform Ops
Pinebridge Analytics

Attachment: Pinebridge_OrderForm_comments.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@pinebridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Order form draft - uptime targets and maintenance

Elena — thanks for the quick read and the annotated copy. Appreciate the concrete asks; here are our initial responses:

- Maintenance windows: we can offer a customer-preferred window for non-emergency maintenance within a 4-hour band and will commit to giving 14 days' notice for planned maintenance. For emergency patches that require immediate action, we will limit such windows to under 2 hours and notify you ASAP.

- Uptime credits: we can agree to an explicit calculation. Proposal: monthly credits are calculated as ((Monthly target - Actual uptime) / Monthly target) * Monthly recurring charges, with a per-incident cap of 25% of monthly fees and a cumulative cap of 50% per month. We can surface the math in the order form appendix.

- Response times: P1 initial response within 30 minutes (acknowledgement and triage), target RTO updates every 2 hours until mitigation. Escalation path: Support -> On-call Infra -> Engineering lead -> VP Eng.

I copied Laura for legal redline coordination and Marcus for ops confirmation on the maintenance flexibility. If this aligns, we can produce a redline that embeds the credit formula and the maintenance scheduling clause.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: Redwood_OrderForm_redlines_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Pinebridge Legal <legal@pinebridge.com>

Subject: RE: Redwood Order form draft - uptime targets and maintenance

Alex/Laura — attaching Pinebridge's redlines (legal perspective). Two items legal will not accept as written:

• 'Force majeure' scope for maintenance: the clause is too broad. We need explicit exclusions for scheduled maintenance with notice, and require a mechanism to dispute any reliance on force majeure for availability impacts.

• Credits methodology: define whether credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for availability failures and include a hard cap. Our procurement counsel prefers a cumulative cap equal to 50% of monthly fees and language that credits are the exclusive remedy for service availability only — not for data loss or security incidents.

We propose a short call with Redwood legal to iron out language. Our availability: Wed/Thu this week in the mornings (ET).

—Sara Kim
Counsel, Pinebridge Legal

Attachment: Pinebridge_Legal_redlines_trackchanges.docx (docx)

Sara/Elena — thanks for the track changes and the availability. I'm Redwood's commercial counsel and I'll take point on the redline session. Quick summary of what we plan to bring to the call so we make efficient use of your time: 

- Narrow force majeure language to explicitly exclude planned maintenance and provide a dispute mechanism (mutual SOC style escalation).

- Insert the uptime credit formula Alex proposed into the order form appendix, and add both the per-incident cap (25%) and cumulative monthly cap (50%) as negotiated. We'll also add plain-language examples so your procurement team can easily validate calculations.

- Confirm response SLAs: P1 ack within 30 minutes; SLA credit triggers will be tied to monitoring window aligned to UTC calendar months. We'll propose a definition for 'availability' that excludes scheduled, notified maintenance and customer-induced outages.

Next steps: Laura to host a 30-minute redline call Thurs 09:00-09:30 ET — I'll send a calendared invite and a clean draft with tracked language to the Drive link prior to the call. Marcus, please confirm that the maintenance scheduling flexibility is operationally feasible and whether we should limit customer-driven windows to a quota per quarter.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
